| IS23-082 | Common fetal indications for fetal echocardiography: suspected cardiac structural anomaly; extracardiac structural anomaly with a known association with congenital heart disease; suspected abnormal function or cardiomegaly; hydrops; persistent tachycardia (180 bpm or more); suspected heart block or persistent bradycardia (110 bpm or less); frequent or persistently irregular rhythm; nuchal translucency 3.5 mm or more; confirmed or suspected genetic abnormality; monochorionic twinning (if resources allow). | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Fetal factors', p. 797 | ai-extracted | |
| IS23-083 | Common patient or familial indications: congenital heart disease in a first-degree relative of the fetus (parents, siblings and half-siblings); first- or second-degree relative with Mendelian disease and childhood cardiac manifestations; pregestational diabetes regardless of HbA1c; anti-Ro/SSA antibodies; phenylketonuria (unknown status or periconceptional phenylalanine above 10 mg/dL); retinoid exposure; confirmed fetal infection (TORCH or parvovirus B19). | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Patient or familial disease or environmental exposure', p. 797 | ai-extracted | |
| IS23-084 | Fetal echocardiography may be considered for: second-degree relative with congenital heart disease; gestational diabetes diagnosed in the first or early second trimester; nuchal translucency 3.0-3.4 mm; selected teratogens (for example paroxetine, carbamazepine, lithium, sodium valproate); conception by IVF including ICSI; use of ACE inhibitors. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Other indications when fetal echo may be considered', p. 797 | ai-cross-checked | |
| IS23-085 | Evidence is insufficient that the risk of congenital heart disease is significantly above baseline for: obesity (BMI 35 kg/m2 or more), SSRI exposure other than paroxetine, non-cardiac soft markers for aneuploidy, abnormal serum analytes, isolated single umbilical artery, gestational diabetes diagnosed after the second trimester, warfarin or alcohol exposure, echogenic intracardiac focus, prenatal fever or viral infection with seroconversion only, or isolated congenital heart disease in a relative more distant than second degree. | ISUOG-2023-SCREEN: Table 2, 'Other considerations', p. 797 | ai-extracted | |
